title: A rule you can apply
description: Take an unclear phrase apart, change it and come back to the same rule on new examples.

blocks.text: The person has a specific question: why the verb sits here and how to say the same thing about yesterday. What they need is a short breakdown of their own construction, not the whole textbook chapter.

quote.text: it needs to include more lessons explaining why grammar rules are implemented. For example, where German verbs fall, how they are conjugated, and why

blocks.text: The phrase is broken into parts, with the rule and one contrasting example alongside. After that the learner changes the tense, the grammatical person or the intent. A mistake in the new attempt takes them back to the part of the explanation that needs clearing up.
Bring the rule back into speech

An addition like this makes sense to test inside a course or a speaking app first. A separate library of rules risks becoming one more reference that is rarely opened. The value shows when the explanation helps build the next line unaided.
